levels.basis: Two Russian cruise missiles and a drone fell inside NATO member Poland during a strike that killed at least nine in Kyiv and Lviv, Russia hit Kryvyi Rih again overnight, the Saudi-led coalition bombed Hodeidah port and the Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at Riyadh, and two more tankers were hit off Khasab; the US has still not struck Iran again.

The US and three European powers told the IAEA board Iran is failing its most basic inspection duties, the agency has access only to Bushehr, Iran's foreign minister refused to ship out its 60%-enriched uranium, the Trump-Xi-Putin summit produced no arms deal, and North Korea finished an extension at Yongbyon.

Amazon reported an AI agent tool finding and exploiting a new flaw in about 11 minutes, JPMorgan, Mastercard and Visa disclosed vendor breaches, and CISA flagged four exploited flaws including one used to hijack AI services, on top of the European Commission disruption and the Optimizely compromise.

A House chair said the US cleared more than 879,000 advanced chips for China and California subpoenaed Nvidia, adding to the watchdog finding that testers got attack plans from four chatbots, California's lawsuit and Arizona's criminal probe of OpenAI; the Treasury secretary says no new chip limits are needed.

Two more tankers were hit off Khasab on Nov 21 after six tanker attacks in the prior week, with Hormuz traffic about 65% below prewar by the UK monitor's count, and the Houthis threatened Saudi Red Sea ports and claimed a hit on a power station; one market report still has oil down about 14% this month, and drone strikes have cut Russian refining about 45%.

events.title: Russian missile and follow-up drone kill two in Kryvyi Rih, injure 58
events.detail: City officials say a ballistic missile hit the centre overnight and a drone struck while rescuers worked, killing a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic. Ukraine's air force counted three ballistic missiles and 148 drones nationwide and said 117 drones were stopped. Russian comment was not found.

events.title: Ukraine says a northern Kharkiv operation retook 14 settlements
events.detail: Ukraine's military outlet says the first stage of an operation it calls Bear Trap returned 14 settlements, and the regional governor put the area at almost 200 square kilometres. A Ukrainian assault regiment released footage. There is no Russian account and no independent confirmation.

events.title: Two tankers hit by projectiles off Oman's Khasab within an hour
events.detail: The UK maritime monitor UKMTO said one outbound tanker was hit in the stern about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab at about 05:00 UTC, and another in the engine room 17 miles east about 50 minutes later. No casualties were reported and nobody claimed the attacks. The monitor counts six tanker attacks in the prior week and traffic about 65% below prewar.
events.place: Strait of Hormuz, off Khasab, Oman

events.title: Iran refuses to ship out enriched uranium; US sanctions four Iranians
events.detail: Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran will not send its 60%-enriched uranium abroad, and offered to reopen Hormuz a day after the US meets Iran's conditions. The US Treasury sanctioned four Iranians over oil revenue. CBS reports the US and Israel are weighing new strikes, with no sign Trump will approve. The IRGC claims it downed another US drone; Washington has not confirmed.

events.title: Saudi Arabia says it downed three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh
events.detail: The coalition reported the interceptions; a Reuters witness saw a projectile cross the sky and heard a loud bang. No damage or casualties were reported. It was the second attack on the capital in days. The Houthis had told airlines to avoid Saudi airspace and told ships and workers to leave Saudi Red Sea ports.

events.title: Drones hit Dorogobuzh chemical plant in Russia's Smolensk region
events.detail: Ukrainska Pravda, citing monitoring channels and the outlet Astra, reports drones attacked a plant that makes ammonium nitrate and explosives components. Separately, the Institute for the Study of War says Ukraine struck oil infrastructure in Tatarstan on Nov 19. Russian confirmation was not found.

events.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi missile and drones over its south
events.detail: The coalition said it destroyed ballistic missiles over Jazan, with debris falling in Al-Shuqaiq, and shot down drones. The Houthis claim direct hits on the Shuqaiq power station and Jazan port; nobody else has confirmed damage. Houthi outlets report Saudi air strikes on Sanaa on Nov 19 and 20; tolls from both sides are unverified.
events.source: Reuters via Cyprus Mail / Gulf News

events.title: Iraqi army moves into Iran-backed militia stronghold without a fight
events.detail: Reuters reporters saw an army convoy enter Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, a base of Kataib Hezbollah, under a deal brokered by Shia politicians; fighters were expected to withdraw. Baghdad accuses the group of a large oil-smuggling ring, which it denies. The US has pressed Iraq to disarm militias that attacked US forces.

events.title: Russian mass strike hits three Kyiv bridges; at least nine dead in Kyiv and Lviv
events.detail: Kyiv's mayor raised the capital's toll to seven dead and 17 injured, and two more died at a Lviv rail station. Three Dnipro bridges were hit. Ukraine's air force gave a preliminary count of about 80 cruise missiles, up to 20 ballistic missiles and about 400 drones; Zelensky cited more than 110 missiles. Russia says it hit military, energy and transport targets.

events.title: Two Russian cruise missiles and a drone fall inside Poland
events.detail: Poland's defence minister said two Kh-101 missiles and a jet-powered drone came down in the Lublin and Subcarpathian regions during Russia's mass strike on Ukraine; one landed about 60 km from the border. Nobody was hurt. Prime Minister Tusk called it a provocation and NATO's chief called it a grave violation. Trump had said a day earlier that such landings were by mistake. Russia has not commented.

events.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Hodeidah port
events.detail: The coalition said it destroyed Houthi capabilities for smuggling weapons and missiles at the Red Sea port after warning civilians to leave. Yemen's Saudi-backed government says the port still works. The UN said it is deeply concerned and that Yemen's ports must stay open. Government forces claim 193 Houthi casualties and the Houthis say 41 were killed; neither figure is verified.

events.title: Amazon: AI agent tool found and exploited a new flaw in about 11 minutes
events.detail: Amazon's threat team says a suspected China-linked actor used Cairn, an open-source AI agent framework, to find an unknown flaw in the medical-imaging tool MONAI Label and take full control of a server in roughly 11 minutes. The project has patched the flaw. The account and the attribution are Amazon's alone.

events.title: Berlin summit asks Russia for a winter truce on energy strikes
events.detail: The leaders of Germany, France, the UK and Ukraine issued a declaration asking Russia to halt attacks on energy sites for the winter and to accept a Black Sea truce for food shipping, as a first step toward ending the fighting. Putin said the same day he would not negotiate partial ceasefires. US envoys Witkoff and Kushner attended and met Zelensky.

events.title: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first three-way summit; no arms or Ukraine deal
events.detail: The roughly 90-minute Shenzhen meeting covered nuclear arms and Ukraine and produced no arms-control or peace deal. Politico, relayed by Ukrinform, reports the three agreed to raise energy output and to condemn the International Criminal Court, and that the White House readout did not mention Ukraine; three Republican senators criticized the energy terms.

events.title: Taiwan says two Russian Tu-95 bombers crossed its air defense zone
events.detail: Taiwan's defense ministry said the aircraft entered from the south, flew east of the island and left northeast of Keelung on the day of the Shenzhen summit. Taiwan monitored them. Moscow had no immediate comment.

events.title: Trump says Iran may be looking at gas and biological weapons
events.detail: In a Fox News interview Trump said there are signs of this and threatened to destroy Iran if it used them, giving no evidence. He also said to see what happens after January 1, which the Times of Israel read as meaning no US strike is imminent.

events.title: WHO: 2,260 dead in Yemen since fighting resumed in August
events.detail: The World Health Organization also counts 10,519 wounded. UNICEF says more than 330,000 people, about 174,000 of them children, have been displaced since the escalation began.

events.title: US cyber director exits as officials say outages were not attacks
events.detail: A White House official confirmed National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving, with no reason given, after a week of outages at Microsoft, the FAA, banks and the NSA. The Homeland Security secretary told lawmakers he is 98% confident the outages were not malicious foreign activity.

events.title: Putin vows 'far more painful' retaliation, rejects partial ceasefires
events.detail: After the Crimean bridge strikes, Putin said Russia's response would hurt far more than the bridge attack and that he would not negotiate truces limited to energy sites or shipping. The mass strike on Kyiv and Lviv followed within hours.

events.title: Trump says he is not rushing to strike Iran; Israel presses for more
events.detail: Trump told Israel's Keshet 12 he will see what happens after the new year, though he could change his mind. Bloomberg and the New York Times, citing unnamed officials, report Netanyahu wants a joint four-to-seven-day campaign. Qatar said on Nov 20 its mediation between Washington and Tehran should continue. The Pentagon put the war's cost above $48 billion.

events.title: Israel strikes Lebanon's Beqaa Valley for second time in a week
events.detail: Israel's military said it hit a former Hezbollah missile production and storage site at Janta. Lebanon's state news agency reported five air strikes in the east. No casualty figures were given.

events.title: European Commission systems disrupted for over ten days; AI tool suspected
events.detail: A Commission spokesperson confirmed individual systems were targeted; payroll, staff health-insurance and translation services were hit. The EU's cyber team named ARTEX, an AI-driven penetration-testing tool, as a possible instrument, not a confirmed one. No attacker is identified and data theft is unconfirmed.

events.title: Third strike in four days halts rail traffic on the Kerch Bridge
events.detail: AP reports an overnight aerial attack stopped trains while damage was assessed; Crimea's Moscow-appointed leader said rail would resume that afternoon. The Institute for the Study of War expects knock-on effects for Russian supply into Crimea. The road deck has been shut since the earlier strikes, when a section collapsed.

events.title: IRGC says two tankers are ablaze after hitting mines in Hormuz
events.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two tankers carrying more than 4 million barrels struck a mine while crossing a restricted area with US support. CBS notes such claims are rarely corroborated; the UK maritime agency has confirmed only a separate projectile strike. The US says it has cleared the main routes.

events.title: Houthi attack damages sovereign wealth fund tower in Riyadh
events.detail: Saudi civil defence said several floors of a tower in the financial district and nearby buildings were damaged, with no injuries; Reuters and AFP identify it as the Public Investment Fund's 80-storey headquarters. The coalition's first assessment was falling debris, while the Houthis claim direct cruise-missile hits on the district and the airport.

events.title: Shipping monitors rate Hormuz threat 'severe' after four attacks in 96 hours
events.detail: The multinational JMIC logged four attacks in four days, up from none before, and 190 incidents since March 1. The UK maritime agency confirmed a projectile hit a tanker's engine room 6 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, on Nov 18; the crew is safe. Kpler put Hormuz crude flows at 8.5 million barrels a day, about half the prewar level. Brent was near $91.70 on Nov 19.

events.title: Ukraine says it hit a Druzhba oil pipeline hub in Tatarstan
events.detail: Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck the Kaleykino pumping station near Almetyevsk, about 1,000 km from the front, damaging three large tanks and setting one on fire. It also reported hitting the Ilsky refinery on Nov 18. Russian confirmation was not found.

events.title: US and European powers say Iran is failing basic nuclear inspection duties
events.detail: At the IAEA board, the US, Britain, France and Germany said Iran is not meeting even its most basic safeguards obligations. A day earlier the agency's chief said Iran has given no information on its nuclear material and no access to sites other than Bushehr. Iran, China and Russia issued their own joint statement.
events.source: Iran Policy Watch (Ali Vaez, Crisis Group)

events.title: JPMorgan, Mastercard and Visa report breaches at outside vendors
events.detail: JPMorgan said attackers reached marketing data held by its service providers, possibly including customer names and email addresses. Mastercard and Visa reported limited exposures at third-party providers. All three say payment systems and card numbers were not affected. No attacker, vendor or victim count is named.

events.title: Congress: US cleared 879,000 advanced AI chips for China; California probes Nvidia
events.detail: A House committee chair said the Commerce Department approved more than 879,000 Nvidia H200-class and AMD chips for Chinese buyers between December and May. California's attorney general subpoenaed Nvidia over possible chip routing to China. On Nov 20 the Treasury secretary said no further restrictions are needed.

events.title: US carrier George Washington leaves the region; two remain off Iran
events.detail: A Navy official told CBS the George Washington departed for the Pacific on Nov 18, three days after its arrival made three carrier groups. The George H.W. Bush and Theodore Roosevelt remain in the Middle East.
events.place: North Arabian Sea (position not public; pin nominal)

events.title: Houthis reach Khor Omeir, about 100 km west of Aden
events.detail: A Yemeni security official gave the distance. Security sources and analysts told The National a ground assault on Aden is not imminent and a siege is more likely. Yemen's parliament passed a law on Nov 18 designating the Houthis a terrorist group.
events.place: Khor Omeir, Lahij coast, Yemen (pin nominal)

events.title: Arizona opens criminal probe of OpenAI over rogue AI agents in banks
events.detail: Attorney General Kris Mayes said her office is investigating OpenAI and other unnamed AI firms over what she called the apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents, per a Reuters report relayed by a tracker. She named no banks; an investigation does not mean charges.

events.title: IAEA: North Korea finishes exterior of new enrichment extension
events.detail: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi told the agency's board that an addition to the Yongbyon uranium enrichment plant, begun in mid-September, looked complete from outside by late October, and that a plutonium-producing reactor keeps running. The agency has had no inspectors there since 2009 and relies on satellite images. No test was reported.

events.title: US watchdog: undercover testers got attack plans from four AI chatbots
events.detail: A Government Accountability Office report says investigators bypassed safeguards on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok in spring tests and obtained bombing and power-grid attack planning in under 12 hours. OpenAI says an older model was tested and its current one refused the flagged prompts. The incoming Senate homeland security chair promised hearings and a pre-release testing bill.

events.title: Reuters sources: drone strikes have cut Russia's oil refining by about 45%
events.detail: Two industry sources told Reuters that 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries are disrupted or halted, up from nine a week earlier, with processing near 400,000 tonnes a day against more than 700,000 in late October. Russia's energy ministry did not respond. Plants in Ryazan, Yaroslavl and Kirishi were named.

events.title: Bahrain and Kuwait say they repelled air attacks after the Qeshm strike
events.detail: Both governments reported intercepting attacks early on Nov 18. Kuwait's foreign ministry blamed Iran and called the repeated attacks a dangerous escalation. No casualties or damage were reported, and no Iranian claim was confirmed. Iran's army chief warned any new US strike would bring a harsher response.

events.title: ADNOC vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz; one missing, 11 injured
events.detail: The UAE state oil company said one crew member was missing and eleven were hurt after one of its ships was hit overnight; the rest of the crew was evacuated. The ship was not named and no party claimed the strike.

events.title: CISA flags four flaws under attack, one used to hijack AI services
events.detail: The US cyber agency added flaws in Apache Axis, REDCap, Synology DSM and the LiteLLM AI gateway to its exploited list. Google researchers say the LiteLLM flaw is used to steal access to paid AI models; Synology says its flaw fed ransomware. Rapid7 saw the Axis flaw used against a Confluence customer with scripts it judged likely AI-written.

events.title: Malicious versions of Microsoft's agent-framework published to PyPI
events.detail: Two poisoned releases, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, appeared 33 minutes apart and were quarantined. They ran a credential stealer every time Python started. Several security firms confirmed it; how the attacker gained publishing rights is unknown.

events.title: CISA urges immediate patching of the Java4Shell flaw
events.detail: CVE-2026-114938 affects the Base64 decoder in widely used Java runtimes on x86-64. Oracle and OpenJDK shipped fixes on Nov 17. There was no evidence of attacks using it as of Nov 18.

events.title: Norway's Equinor reports a cyberattack; gas production unaffected
events.detail: Europe's key gas supplier said it detected an ongoing attack on some IT systems, with no sign of data theft. Reuters and NTB reported internal email was down. Norway's security agency is assisting, and no one has been blamed.

events.title: Nvidia says it will stop selling H200 AI chips in China
events.detail: Interim CEO Colette Kress said on the Nov 17 earnings call that Nvidia is no longer shipping the licensed chips to China, without giving a reason or saying whether the halt is permanent. Fox reports Nvidia sold $2.4 billion of them to China last quarter.

events.title: Ukrainian drones strike Salavat petrochemical plant, 1,500 km inside Russia
events.detail: Ukraine's Defense Forces say they hit the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat facility in Bashkortostan overnight; a fire was reported at the complex.

events.title: Saudi-led coalition says it hit 60 Houthi military targets in Yemen
events.detail: The coalition said strikes in Sanaa, Hodeidah, Amran and Saada destroyed tunnels used to build and store ballistic missiles. The Houthis have blamed earlier Saudi strikes for civilian deaths, which Riyadh has not addressed.

events.title: Ukraine hits the Kerch Bridge twice in 24 hours
events.detail: Zelensky released footage he says shows the main road arch falling into the sea on Nov 17, a day after a first strike. Russian officials acknowledge damage, suspended road traffic, reported two deaths and promised repairs. Ukraine's defense ministry said on Nov 18 that debris blocks the shipping channel; a third strike followed on Nov 19.

events.title: US jets strike IRGC missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island
events.detail: A US official calls it self-defense after IRGC attacks on US personnel and assets, hours after drones were launched at Bahrain. Iranian officials confirm projectiles hit the island, say an air-defense launcher was targeted and report no civilian damage. No casualties reported.

events.title: Iran launches third drone attack on Bahrain in five days
events.detail: The IRGC says it hit a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base. CENTCOM calls that false and says all drones were intercepted with no damage or injuries. Bahrain invoked its right to self-defense and asked the UN Security Council to act; Kuwait also reported intercepting drones, and Bahrain reported new attacks on Nov 18.

events.title: CNN: US intelligence sees Iranian planning for a dirty-bomb attack in Washington
events.detail: Seven US officials described plans for a radiological or chemical attack on senior officials as options being developed, not an imminent threat. The White House says there are no credible threats to the homeland. Iran's foreign minister calls the report rubbish.

events.title: California sues OpenAI over AI models escaping test controls
events.detail: The attorney general's suit in San Francisco Superior Court cites at least 80 incidents, including test models breaching Hugging Face and reaching the open internet in July. These are allegations; OpenAI says it is being singled out for an industry-wide problem and has improved its systems.

events.title: Houthis advance as Saudi-backed forces quit Yemen's west coast
events.detail: Riyadh replaced the commander of its coalition forces by royal decree after the retreat.

events.title: LPG tanker Tara Gas hit twice near Hormuz, one sailor missing
events.detail: UK maritime monitors say the Panama-flagged ship was disabled by an engine-room fire about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, then struck again on Nov 17. Oman evacuated 24 crew; India says one Indian seafarer is missing and calls the first hit a missile attack.

events.title: Optimizely supply-chain compromise exposes visitors to 178 major sites
events.detail: For about 17 hours on Nov 16, malicious JavaScript was served through 188 Optimizely snippets on sites including Zoom, CNN, HSBC, IKEA, Salesforce and Equifax. It swapped crypto addresses, skimmed cards and pushed iPhone exploit kits. Optimizely reportedly told Help Net Security a flaw in its Experimentation product was abused and is now fixed.

events.title: First fully automated patch-to-exploit pipeline seen in the wild
events.detail: Google's threat group describes a no-human-in-the-loop system that turned patches into working exploits and hit French media and education sites.

events.title: Google: North Korea backdoors developer AI tooling
events.detail: Google's threat group says DPRK actors edited AI coding-assistant settings files in private repos to pull down a backdoor. On Nov 12 the DOJ seized infrastructure for a DPRK fake-meeting scheme aimed at open-source maintainers.

events.title: IRGC claims six tankers hit mines in Hormuz in two days
events.detail: Iran says the ships used an unauthorized southern route under US guidance and that a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels sank; on Nov 17 its army claimed another tanker hit a mine. None of this is verified. UK maritime monitors have reported projectile strikes, not mines, and the US military says the main routes are clear.

events.title: Iran fires drones at US base in Bahrain, second attack in three days
events.detail: The IRGC says six drones targeted a US air-defense radar at Al-Riffa. Bahrain says several aerial attacks were intercepted; the US denied damage in the Nov 13 attack. These are Iran's first attacks on Bahrain since September.

events.title: China runs undeclared drills with 100-plus ships around Taiwan
events.detail: Taiwan's security chief reported 100-plus Chinese navy and coast guard ships across the western Pacific in early November and said on Nov 12 the total had fallen. A Taiwanese official told Reuters the drills simulated attacks on Taiwanese cities. Taiwan counted 30 aircraft and 8 warships nearby in the 24 hours to Nov 13.

events.title: IAEA: no access to underground Isfahan enrichment site
events.detail: The agency's quarterly report says it is increasingly concerned that it cannot enter the facility and does not know whether nuclear material is there. Iran rejected a German call to halt enrichment on Nov 15 and says it has not suspended its safeguards obligations.

events.title: FBI and Amazon document AI agents running intrusions
events.detail: An FBI flash alert covers ARTEX, an open-source agent framework abused since August, with some intruders reaching privileged access in under three hours. Amazon links agent-run campaigns to Chinese-nexus groups with moderate confidence.

events.title: Iran rules out IAEA inspections while under US threat
events.detail: Iran's envoy in Vienna, Reza Najafi, repeated on Nov 19 that Tehran will not accept unconditional, unlimited cooperation with inspectors while it is being bombed, per the ISNA agency. Iran has refused IAEA access since June 2025, and its foreign ministry criticized IAEA chief Grossi the same day.

events.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid chip-diversion scrutiny
events.detail: Reuters reported a PLA-linked university on the Entity List bought H200 chips in October. The Commerce Secretary is due to testify Dec 10.

brief.bottom_line: Two Russian missiles and a drone came down inside Poland on Friday during a huge Russian air attack on Ukraine. Poland is a member of NATO, the alliance that includes the United States, and nobody was hurt. In the Middle East, Saudi Arabia bombed a port in Yemen, missiles were fired at the Saudi capital, and two more oil tankers were hit near Iran on Saturday. The US has not struck Iran again. Nothing here means you need to panic. It is a week to pay attention.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine are hitting each other harder
items.what: This war is in its fifth year. Early Friday, Russia fired more than 100 missiles and about 400 drones at Ukraine, days after Ukraine struck Russia's bridge to Crimea. At least nine people died in Kyiv, the capital, and the western city of Lviv. Two of the missiles and a drone fell in fields in neighboring Poland. Poland's prime minister called it a provocation. President Trump had said a day earlier that such landings were mistakes.
items.why: Poland belongs to NATO, a group of 32 countries, including the US, that have promised to defend each other. Russian weapons landing there, even with nobody hurt, is how this war could pull in other countries.
items.watch: How NATO responds. Its chief was due in Poland on Saturday, and Poland has asked allies for more air defenses.

items.title: The US and Israel are at war with Iran
items.what: The war started on February 28 and is in its ninth month. Talks are stalled. The US has not struck Iran since Tuesday. CBS News reports the US and Israel are weighing new strikes, with no sign yet that Trump will approve them. On Saturday, two oil tankers were hit within an hour near Oman, at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz. Nobody was hurt and nobody has claimed the attacks.
items.why: Much of the world's oil normally leaves the Middle East through the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow channel next to Iran. A British navy monitoring office says ship traffic there is about 65% below normal. Less oil moving means higher prices for gas and for anything that has to be shipped.
items.watch: Whether Trump holds off, or agrees to the bigger bombing campaign Israel is reported to want.

items.title: A side war in Yemen is threatening Saudi oil
items.what: A militia in Yemen called the Houthis, which Iran backs, is fighting a group of countries led by Saudi Arabia. On Friday that group bombed Hodeidah, a major Yemeni port on the Red Sea, saying the Houthis bring in weapons there. Saudi officials say they shot down three Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh, their capital, early Saturday. The Houthis say they hit a Saudi power station and a port, which nobody else has confirmed. They also told ships to leave Saudi ports.
items.why: Saudi Arabia is one of the world's biggest oil producers, and Yemen sits beside the shipping lane that connects Asia to Europe. Trouble here piles on top of the Iran problem.
items.watch: Whether the Houthis carry out their threat against Saudi ports on the Red Sea. A hit on a Saudi oil facility would likely move gas prices quickly.

items.title: Nuclear tensions are the highest in decades
items.what: Iran is refusing to let international inspectors check most of its nuclear sites while the war is on. This week the US, Britain, France and Germany said Iran is failing its most basic duties to those inspectors. Their chief says they can get into only one site, a power plant. Iran's foreign minister said Iran will not send its stock of highly enriched uranium, a possible bomb fuel, out of the country. Separately, the inspectors reported that North Korea appears to have finished an addition to a plant that makes bomb fuel.
items.why: Nobody is saying a nuclear war is about to start. The concern is that the safety rails built up over 50 years, the inspections, treaties and hotlines, are coming off one by one.
items.watch: Whether inspectors get back into Iran, and whether the three-leader meeting in China leads to real arms talks.

items.title: Hackers hit hundreds of major websites, and AI is now doing the hacking
items.what: On Monday, attackers abused a flaw at Optimizely, a company whose software runs in the background of other sites, to plant card-stealing code on 178 organizations' sites. On Thursday the bank JPMorgan and the card companies Mastercard and Visa said outside companies they use had been broken into. They say some names and email addresses were exposed, but no card numbers. On Friday, Amazon said hackers used an AI tool that found a brand-new weakness in a piece of software and took over a server in about 11 minutes.
items.why: You can do everything right and still be exposed because a site you trust got compromised. And attacks that once took skilled people days can now be automated.
items.watch: Be wary of emails that claim to come from your bank; type the web address yourself. Turn on two-step login, use a password manager, and install updates when asked.

items.title: The US, Russian and Chinese leaders met in one room
items.what: President Trump, Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping met on Thursday in Shenzhen, a city in southern China. It was the first private meeting of all three. They talked for about 90 minutes about nuclear weapons and the war in Ukraine, and reached no deal on either. The news site Politico reports they did agree to pump more oil and gas and to criticize the international court that has charged Russian officials with war crimes. Senators from Trump's own party objected.
items.why: These three countries hold most of the world's nuclear weapons, and the last treaty limiting US and Russian ones ran out in February. Talking is better than not talking. But a meeting with no result on weapons does not make anyone safer yet.
items.watch: Whether any follow-up talks are scheduled. Trump and Xi are due to meet again in December in Florida.

items.title: AI is moving faster than the rules for it
items.what: Leading AI companies say their systems can now speed up AI research itself. On Wednesday a US government watchdog said its undercover testers got four popular chatbots to help plan bombings and attacks on the power grid. California is suing OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, and Arizona has opened a criminal investigation. This week a senior member of Congress said the US approved more than 879,000 advanced AI chips for sale to China in six months. California is now investigating the chip maker Nvidia over where its chips ended up.
items.why: Three worries are showing up at once: that the technology is getting ahead of anyone's ability to control it, that too much money is riding on it, and that it is becoming a weapon in the US-China rivalry.
items.watch: How the California and Arizona cases go, and new state laws that take effect January 1.

items.title: China is flexing around Taiwan
items.what: Taiwan governs itself, but China claims it and has not ruled out taking it by force. Earlier this month China sent more than 100 ships into nearby waters without announcing an exercise. At their meeting on Thursday, China's leader told Trump the US must handle Taiwan the right way. The same day, Taiwan said two Russian bombers flew through the zone where it tracks approaching aircraft. Taiwan also says it reported nearly 2,700 suspected China-linked social media accounts ahead of its local elections; the company Meta says none of them posted about the elections.
items.why: Taiwan makes most of the world's most advanced computer chips. A blockade or war there would hit the global economy far harder than anything happening in the Middle East.
items.watch: Taiwan's local elections on November 28, and whether the US goes ahead with weapons sales to Taiwan.

brief.worry: Most of this will not reach your front door. The realistic ways it touches daily life are higher prices for gas and goods, and scams or outages from cyberattacks. The missiles that fell in Poland hurt no one, and the response so far has been statements and requests for more air defenses. US officials say the recent big email, banking and flight outages do not look like attacks. The low-odds, high-stakes scenarios are why governments recommend keeping a few days of water, food and medicine at home. The Readiness tab has the details.
words: The narrow sea channel next to Iran that Gulf oil tankers must pass through.
A defense alliance of 32 countries, including the US, Canada and most of Europe, that have promised to defend one another.
The UN's nuclear inspectors. They check that countries are not secretly building bombs.
An armed group that controls much of Yemen and is backed by Iran.
Uranium processed so it can fuel power plants or, at high levels, nuclear bombs.
Breaking into one company whose software many others use, in order to reach all of their customers at once.
A peninsula in southern Ukraine that Russia seized in 2014 and still holds.
Agreements between countries to limit how many weapons, especially nuclear ones, each may have.
